jobs.description:

English language skills are required. Danish is an advantage.

Full-time position.

Permanent employment.

Salary based on qualifications.

Please send your CV and application to:

 job@vejentil.dk

About Us Tandoori Twist is an offering from Tinyhus Cafe, a child-friendly cafe in Copenhagen, Denmark, serving authentic Indian delicacies.    We serve not only classic favourites like butter chicken and biriyani, but also lesser known Indian regional food, with myriad of spices and flavours as our specilities. We strive to provide authentic food and exceptional service to our guests and we look for team members who are self-motivated, proactive and passionate to walk the extra mile to provide exceptional culinery experience for our guests.  
Our people, just like our food, are the ambassadors of our cafe and restaurant. You can work in a fast-paced environment, flexible and efficient in juggling multiple tasks typical for a small but growing organisation

Prior experience in working in an Asian / Indian kitchen is highly advantageous

jobs.occupation: Postdoc in BioPhysics
jobs.description:
Many microorganisms, such as bacteria and cancer cells, exhibit remarkable collective dynamics, often described as "living liquids" or active fluids, and arise due to local internal energy injection. Likeconventional liquids, the macro-scale confinement, or boundaries, of thfluid can control their flow patterns, and the micro-scale behaviour of the microorganisms.  However, many physical systems exist within a deformable environment such as the mucus layers in the body.

  As a result, not only does this living liquid get affected by its environment, but it can also reshape its soft surroundings as a form of mechanoreciprocity. This leads to a range of fascinating phenomena, such as cancer cells invading surrounding extracellular matrix, soil-dwelling bacteria burrowing through sand, and the infection of mucus by pathogenic bacteria. This research project will use computational models to explore the bidirectional relationship between an organism’s motility and its adaptable environment, investigating how microorganisms not only adapt to, but also actively restructure their surroundings.

  This application is posted with a corresponding PhD position and only one of the positions will be filled. We are looking for candidates interested in biophysical systems and computational physics, with a preference for some knowledge about programming.

  The postdoc’s duties will include research within biophysics as well as teaching. The post may also include performance of other duties.

  Further information on the Department is linked at the NBI website. Inquiries about the position can be made to Kristian Thijssen, Kristian.thijssen@nbi.ku.dk. 

  Terms of employment
 The two-year position is open from 1 Nov 2026 or as soon as possible thereafter.

  The position is covered by the Memorandum on Job Structure for Academic Staff.

  Terms of appointment and payment accord to the agreement between the Ministry of Finance and The Danish Confederation of Professional Associations on Academics in the State.

  Negotiation for salary supplement is possible.

  The application, in English, must be submitted electronically through UCPH Job Portal.

  When you will be affiliated with the University of Copenhagen or otherwise have access to their research, you may be required to undergo a background screening. The purpose is to protect the security and research integrity of the University of Copenhagen.

  Please include 

   	
• Curriculum vitae 	
• Diplomas (Master and PhD degree or equivalent) 	
• 1 page Research plan,  description of current and future research plans 	
• Complete publication list 	
• Separate reprints of 3 particularly relevant papers   The deadline for applications is 31 August 2026, 23.59 (CEST)
 After the expiry of the deadline for applications, the authorized recruitment manager selects applicants for assessment on the advice of the Interview Committee. 

  You can read about the recruitment process here.

   

  The University wishes our staff to reflect the diversity of society and thus welcomes applications from all qualified candidates regardless of personal background.

jobs.occupation: Dygtigt faglært kok søges. // skilled trained chef or a chef with equivalent international experience
jobs.description:
English below: 

Kok Søges Til Væveriet

Vi søger en dygtig faglært kok eller en kok med tilsvarende udenlandsk erfaring til Væveriet i Dalbygade.

Vi er hovedsageligt et eventkøkken, men laver også kokkeskoler, teambuilding, mad over bål i de varme sæsoner og en god del grill. Vi kører ikke faste, låste menuer året rundt, så der er plads til kreativitet, egne idéer og de retter, du selv brænder for at lave.

Vi er et lille hold med et stærkt sammenhold. Her løfter vi i flok, hjælper hinanden og har det godt sammen, også når tempoet stiger.

Vi leder efter dig, der:

• 
Er faglært kok eller har tilsvarende udenlandsk erfaring.

• 
Er rigtig god til at lave mad.

• 
Har et solidt grundrepertoire og ikke skal starte med opskriften hver gang.

• 
Har interesse for råvarer, smag og god afvikling.

• 
Kan holde aftaler og møde forberedt.

• 
Er en god kollega og bidrager til fællesskabet.

• 
Har fornuftig fysik og er klar på at knokle, når der er travlt.

• 
Har humor og kan holde hovedet koldt.

• 
Er fleksibel med arbejdstiderne.

• 
Ikke går i panik, fordi der pludselig har sneget sig en ekstra veganer, allergiker eller FODMAP-gæst ind i selskabet.

Du behøver ikke have 15 års erfaring. Det vigtigste er, at du kan dit håndværk, har lyst til at udvikle dig og elsker følelsen af, at et travlt køkken bare spiller.

Vi er skarpe på tidsplaner, afvikling og varm mad til mange mennesker. Samtidig er vi et hus, hvor der sker meget, så du skal være med på, at vi hjælper hinanden på tværs, når det giver mening. Til gengæld har vi faktisk ret godt styr på tingene.

Arbejdet ligger naturligvis ofte, når andre har fri. Klargøring og forberedelse kan til gengæld i høj grad planlægges fornuftigt.

Vi tilbyder pension, sundhedsforsikring, feriepenge og løn efter kompetencer og ansvarsområder. Arbejder du mange lørdage, tager vi selvfølgelig også en snak om, at lønnen skal afspejle det.

Tiltrædelse snarest, men vi venter gerne på den rigtige profil.

Send en ansøgning til rasmus@vaeveriet.com.

Chef Wanted At Væveriet

We are looking for a skilled trained chef or a chef with equivalent international experience to join Væveriet in Dalbygade.

We are primarily an event kitchen, but we also run cooking classes, teambuilding events, open-fire cooking in the warmer seasons and quite a bit of grilling. We do not work with fixed, locked menus all year round, so there is room for creativity, your own ideas and the dishes you genuinely enjoy making.

We are a small team with a strong sense of community. We help each other, lift together and keep the mood good, even when things get busy.

We are looking for someone who:

• 
Is a trained chef or has equivalent international experience.

• 
Is genuinely good at cooking.

• 
Has a solid basic repertoire and does not need to start from a recipe every time.

• 
Cares about ingredients, flavour and smooth service.

• 
Keeps agreements and shows up prepared.

• 
Is a good colleague and contributes to the team.

• 
Has decent physical stamina and is ready to work hard when needed.

• 
Has a sense of humour and can keep calm under pressure.

• 
Is flexible with working hours.

• 
Does not panic when an extra vegan, allergy or FODMAP guest suddenly appears on the function sheet.

You do not need 15 years of experience. What matters most is that you know your craft, want to develop and enjoy the feeling of a busy kitchen running well.

We are sharp on timing, execution and serving hot food to large groups. At the same time, Væveriet is a place where many things happen, so you should be willing to help across the house when it makes sense. In return, we are actually quite structured and usually have a good grip on things.

The work naturally often takes place when other people are off. Prep and planning, however, can usually be arranged in a sensible way.

We offer pension, health insurance, holiday pay and salary based on skills and areas of responsibility. If you work many Saturdays, we will of course discuss a salary that reflects that.

Start as soon as possible, but we are happy to wait for the right profile.

Send your application to rasmus@vaeveriet.com.

jobs.occupation: PhD Fellowship in BioPhysics
jobs.description:
The Niels Bohr Institute, Faculty of Science at University of Copenhagen invites applicants for a PhD fellowship in computational modelling of active materials and their environment

  Start date is (expected to be) 1 December 2026.

  The project
 Many microorganisms, such as bacteria and cancer cells, exhibit remarkable collective dynamics, often described as "living liquids" or active fluids, and arise due to local internal energy injection. Likeconventional liquids, the macro-scale confinement, or boundaries, of thfluid can control their flow patterns, and the micro-scale behaviour of the microorganisms.  However, many physical systems exist within a deformable environment such as the mucus layers in the body.

  As a result, not only does this living liquid get affected by its environment, but it can also reshape its soft surroundings as a form of mechanoreciprocity. This leads to a range of fascinating phenomena, such as cancer cells invading surrounding extracellular matrix, soil-dwelling bacteria burrowing through sand, and the infection of mucus by pathogenic bacteria. This research project will use computational models to explore the bidirectional relationship between an organism’s motility and its adaptable environment, investigating how microorganisms not only adapt to, but also actively restructure their surroundings.

  This application is posted with a corresponding Postdoc position and only one of the positions will be filled.

  Who are we looking for?
 We are looking for candidates interested in biophysical systems and computational physics, with preference for some knowledge about programming.

  Our group and research- and what do we offer?
 As a newly established research group, we utilize state-of-the-art computational models to study pattern formation in microorganisms. By combining discrete solvers, particularly a particle-based mesoscale hydrodynamic solver known as MPCD, with continuum simulations, we aim to characterize the collective dynamics of biological matter, their hydrodynamic interactions, and their influence on adaptable environments. This multiscale approach enables us to explore active systems that actively restructure their surroundings as effective ecosystem engineers.    

  We offer a highly creative and collaborative research atmosphere at the interface between physics, biology and fluid mechanics. Our research facilitates high performance computing facilities and actively encourage cooperation and or collaboration with the researchers who develop the numerical solvers used. The PhD fellowship is given in accordance with Danish legislation and will typically run for 3 years. The salary is set accordingly to Danish Union Contracts which are very competitive within the international academic community.

  Principal supervisor is Dr. Kristian Thijssen, Niels Bohr Institute, kristian.thijssen@nbi.ku.dk.

  Qualifications needed for the PhD programme
 To be eligible for the regular PhD programme, you must have completed a degree programme, equivalent to a Danish master’s degree (180 ECTS/3 FTE BSc + 120 ECTS/2 FTE MSc) related to the subject area of the project, e.g. Physics. For information of eligibility of completed programmes, see General assessments for specific countries and Assessment database.

  Terms of employment
 Employment as PhD fellow is full time and for maximum 3 years.

  Employment is conditional upon your successful enrolment as a PhD student at the PhD School at the Faculty of SCIENCE, University of Copenhagen. This requires submission and acceptance of an application for the specific project formulated by the applicant.

  The terms of employment and salary are in accordance to the agreement between the Ministry of Finance and The Danish Confederation of Professional Associations on Academics in the State (AC). The position is covered by the Protocol on Job Structure.

  Responsibilities and tasks

   	
• Carry through an independent research project under supervision 	
• Complete PhD courses corresponding to approx. 30 ECTS / ½ FTE 	
• Participate in active research environments, including a stay at another research institution, preferably abroad 	
• Teaching and knowledge dissemination activities 	
• Write scientific papers aimed at high-impact journals 	
• Write and defend a PhD thesis on the basis of your project   We are looking for the following qualifications:

   	
• Professional qualifications relevant to the PhD project 	
• Relevant publications 	
• Relevant work experience 	
• Other relevant professional activities 	
• Curious mind-set with a strong interest in soft matter systems 	
• Good language skills   Application and Assessment Procedure
 Your application including all attachments must be in English and submitted electronically by clicking APPLY NOW below.

  Please include: 

   	
• Motivated letter of application (max. one page) 	
• Curriculum vitae including information about your education, experience, language skills and other skills relevant for the position 	
• Original diplomas for Bachelor or Master and transcript of records in the original language, including an authorized English translation if issued in another language than English or Danish. If not completed, a certified/signed copy of a recent transcript of records or a written statement from the institution or supervisor is accepted. 	
• Publication list (if possible) 	
• Reference letters (if available)   The deadline for applications is 31 August 2026, 23:59 (CEST)
 We reserve the right not to consider material received after the deadline, and not to consider applications that do not live up to the abovementioned requirements.

  The further process 
 After deadline, a number of applicants will be selected for academic assessment by an unbiased expert assessor. You are notified, whether you will be passed for assessment.

  The assessor will assess the qualifications and experience of the shortlisted applicants with respect to the above mentioned research area, techniques, skills and other requirements. The assessor will conclude whether each applicant is qualified and, if so, for which of the two models. The assessed applicants will have the opportunity to comment on their assessment. You can read about the recruitment process here.

  Interviews with selected candidates are expected to be held in September

  Questions
 For specific information about the PhD fellowship, please contact the principal supervisor.

  General information about PhD study at the Faculty of SCIENCE is available at the PhD School’s website.

   

  The University of Copenhagen wishes to reflect the surrounding community and invites all regardless of personal background to apply for the position.

jobs.occupation: Declaration of interest regarding PhD project: The Molecular Endocrinology Department (KMEB), Department of Clinical Research, University of Southern Denmark (SDU), invites applications for a 3-year PhD scholarship
jobs.description:
Declaration of interest regarding PhD project:

The Molecular Endocrinology Department (KMEB), Department of Clinical Research, University of Southern Denmark (SDU), invites applications for a 3-year PhD scholarship for a highly motivated candidate interested in working at the intersection of cancer biology and endocrinology. The project aims to investigate stanniocalcin-2 (STC2) as a key mediator of adipose tissue–tumor crosstalk in obesity-related cancer.

The project is part of a larger collaborative research initiative, the Molecular Mechanisms Linking Obesity and Cancer (MMLOC) network, funded by the Novo Nordisk Foundation. Though this grant, 2/3 of the PhD salary has been secured.

Employment is therefore conditional upon the successful enrolment of the candidate as a PhD student at the PhD School at Faculty of Health Sciences, and the awarding of a one-year Faculty Scholarship. 

 

Research environment

The PhD project will be anchored at KMEB, a research unit focused on clinical and translational endocrinology, under the supervision of Associate Professor Rikke Hjortebjerg and Professor Jan Frystyk. The project will be conducted in close collaboration with the laboratory of co-supervisor Professor Henrik Ditzel, Cancer and Inflammation Research Unit, Department of Molecular Medicine, SDU. 

The candidate will work across two complementary research groups with access to state-of-the-art research facilities. Together, the groups provide a multidisciplinary research environment with close integration of clinical and experimental research. The teams are internationally oriented and offer a supportive and inclusive research culture.

You can read more about KMEB here: https://www.sdu.dk/en/forskning/kmeb

 

Project description

Our research centers around the insulin-like growth factor (IGF) system, a key hormonal regulator in several diseases. The project focuses on stanniocalcin-2 (STC2), an IGF system member that is linked to poor outcomes in most obesity-related cancers but paradoxically predicts favorable prognosis in postmenopausal estrogen receptor-positive (ER+) breast cancer. 

The aim is to examine how STC2 effects are modulated by obesity and estrogen signaling and how it regulates IGF-2/insulin receptor pathways in the tumor–adipose microenvironment. To establish clinically relevant models, the candidate will generate patient-derived xenograft (PDX) mouse models with human tumor tissue and participate in establishing patient-derived organoids and 3D co-cultures. These systems will be interrogated using genetically engineered STC2 and PAPP-A variants and analyzed with advanced sequencing, spatial, and single-cell omics.

The PhD student will:

• 
Establish and analyze PDX mouse models of ER+ breast cancer.

• 
Sample and process tumor and tumor-adjacent/distant adipose tissue from breast cancer patients.

• 
Assess STC2 activity, IGF-2 signaling, and tumor growth under estrogen-controlled conditions.

• 
Help analyze molecular data generated through sequencing and omics-based approaches.

 

Qualifications

The applicant should possess the following qualifications:

• 
A master’s degree (MSc or equivalent) in molecular biology, biomedicine, or related fields. 

• 
Preferably prior experience with endocrinology or cancer research. 

• 
An interest in working with animal models (mice) is a necessity.

• 
Excellent communication skills in English, both written and spoken.

• 
A motivated, independent, and quality-oriented approach to research, with enthusiasm for learning new scientific disciplines and methodologies.

 

For further information about the project, please contact:
Rikke Hjortebjerg

KMEB, Department of Clinical Research

University of Southern Denmark (SDU)

E-mail: rhjortebjerg@health.sdu.dk

Applications must include:

• At letter stating the interest, motivation and qualifications for the project (max. 2 pages) - upload under “Application form”.
• Detailed CV, including personal contact information
• Certified copy of diploma (Master’s degree in a relevant field)

Further information about the PhD-study can be found at the homepage of the University.

Applications must be submitted electronically using the link "Apply now". Attached files must be in Adobe PDF format. We strongly recommend that you read How to apply for a position at SDU before you apply.

Incomplete applications and applications received after the deadline will neither be considered nor evaluated. This also applies to reference letters.

 

Closing date September 1, 2026

Successful candidates will be asked to send an application to the PhD Secretariat, Faculty of Health Sciences, to be enrolled as PhD students.

The PhD programme will be carried out in accordance with Faculty regulations and the Danish Ministerial Order on the PhD Programme at the Universities (PhD order)

 

Salary and Working Conditions at SDU

PhD students employed at SDU are employed as PhD fellows according to the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations in public employment (AC) agreement.

Salary and any salary supplement are paid according to your seniority level and as negotiated with your union representative. The base salary (excluding 18.07% pension contribution) is DKK 374,912.98.

The University wishes our staff to reflect the diversity of society and thus welcomes applications from all qualified candidates regardless of personal background.
